findings.why_exploitable: Any app can start LoginActivity directly, skipping the screens and checks that normally lead to it.
findings.fix: Set android:exported="false" unless other apps need it; otherwise add android:permission with a signature-level permission.

findings.why_exploitable: Any app can start EntranceActivity directly, skipping the screens and checks that normally lead to it.
findings.fix: Set android:exported="false" unless other apps need it; otherwise add android:permission with a signature-level permission.

findings.why_exploitable: Any app can start MainActivity directly, skipping the screens and checks that normally lead to it.
findings.fix: Set android:exported="false" unless other apps need it; otherwise add android:permission with a signature-level permission.

findings.why_exploitable: Any app can query or modify the exported services and receive the app's identity, so other apps can steal app data.
findings.fix: Set android:exported="false" unless other apps need it; otherwise add android:permission with a signature-level permission.

findings.why_exploitable: Any app can query or modify the private data of other apps through content://oversecured.ovaa.theftoverwrite/oversecured.ovaa.theftoverwrite/credentials, bypassing the PIN screen.
findings.fix: Set android:exported="false" unless other apps need it; otherwise protect it with a signature-level android:permission.

findings.why_exploitable: Anyone can unpack the APK and read BASE_URL; the same value ships to every install and cannot be rotated without an update.
findings.fix: Remove the secret from the app; keep it on the server and issue short-lived, per-user tokens.

findings.evidence: onReceive runs any installed receiver of a given action and executes its code with the app's identity
findings.why_exploitable: Any app can send broadcasts to this receiver and drive its logic with forged extras.
findings.fix: Do not take the app out of the sandbox; keep it on the device and allow only trusted packages to send broadcasts.

findings.evidence: onHandleIntent runs dumpLogs for any sender of the action
findings.why_exploitable: The receiver of the broadcast (any app that sends this action) can register for it and drive the sensitive operation with crafted intents.
findings.fix: Use an explicit intent (setPackage(getPackageName()) or setComponent), a signature permission on send, or an in-process callback.

findings.why_exploitable: Anyone can read the password by decompiling the APK and extracting it, or the password can be guessed.
findings.fix: Remove it from the app; keep secrets server-side or generate keys in the Android Keystore.

findings.why_exploitable: Anyone can unpack the APK and read KEY; the same value ships to every install and cannot be rotated without an update.
findings.fix: Remove the secret from the app; keep it on the server and issue short-lived, per-user tokens.

findings.evidence: on return from startActivityForResult, the caller chooses whether to accept the result or not
findings.why_exploitable: The caller controls whether the result is returned to the caller app or not, so it can obtain the URI itself without a deep link.
findings.fix: Return the result to the caller app, never echo it, and require explicit user confirmation.

findings.why_exploitable: Whoever receives the broadcast (for example through an IntentFilter) runs arbitrary HTML and JavaScript, so the page can steal the token.
findings.fix: Do not launch Intents for non-exported components or send broadcasts to other apps; map intents to inner classes or services only.

findings.evidence: JavaScript-enabled WebView loads the "url" extra into the WebView's view hierarchy
findings.why_exploitable: Attacker-controlled content loaded in this WebView can run script with the app's WebView privileges.
findings.fix: Do not render HTML from intent extras; keep JavaScript off for untrusted content.

findings.evidence: JavaScript-enabled WebView loads the "url" extra into the WebView's view hierarchy
findings.why_exploitable: Attacker-controlled content loaded in this WebView can run script with the app's WebView privileges.
findings.fix: Do not render HTML from intent extras; keep JavaScript off for untrusted content.

findings.evidence: JavaScript-enabled WebView loads any URL passed to it, including file:// URLs
findings.why_exploitable: JavaScript in a file:// page can read other local files (and with universal access, any origin), so a loaded HTML file can steal app data.
findings.fix: Call setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs(false) and serve local content through WebViewAssetLoader over https://appassets.androidplatform.net.

findings.why_exploitable: World-accessible files in the app sandbox can be read or changed by every other app on older Android versions.
findings.fix: Use MODE_PRIVATE; share data with other apps only through a FileProvider with explicit grants.

findings.evidence: writes logcat to get the logs
findings.why_exploitable: Sensitive data is stored where other apps, backups or anyone with device access can read it.
findings.fix: Write sensitive data to getFilesDir() or encrypt it, and share it only through a FileProvider.

findings.evidence: opened with context.openInputStream(uri) and then written to the cache dir
findings.why_exploitable: Sensitive data is stored where other apps, backups or anyone with device access can read it.
findings.fix: Avoid storing it, or encrypt it with a Keystore-backed key (EncryptedSharedPreferences/EncryptedFile) in internal storage.

findings.why_exploitable: This algorithm or mode is broken or deterministic, so encrypted data can be recovered or patterns leak.
findings.fix: Use AES/GCM/NoPadding with a random IV and a Keystore key, SecureRandom for random values, and a slow salted KDF for passwords.
